column4: Archaic and obscure; the meaning 'firmament' is doubtful and it only confuses a learner, while 'span' is already listed.
Duplicate of the loyal follower sense, which is kept in item 1.
Geus is a noun (a Dutch Protestant rebel), not an adjective, and the 'belonging' gloss is meaningless; the Protestant sense is already listed in item 5.
'To like' (as in 'het bevalt me') is an archaic usage of gevallen that only confuses learners, and it is not a real everyday sense.
The meadows sense is obscure/dubious and only confuses a learner; the real meaning is entrails, kept in the other item.
'Hawker' is not a meaning of glazenmaker; it is probably a mix-up with a different word (a 'glazenmaker' is also a dragonfly, but not a hawker).
'To stare' is not a real meaning of gluipen, which means to lurk or sneak, so this entry is wrong and overlaps with the other.
Sports champion is not a real meaning of godenzoon; at most a figurative use of the first sense.
Archaic sense with a vague gloss 'action' that duplicates the single real meaning of denying God.
Archaic term that duplicates the other 'Peace of God' meaning and only confuses a learner.
New World sparrow is a narrower subset of the bunting meaning and mostly duplicates it.
'Plain' is not a meaning of gors in modern Dutch (it is an archaic/dialect word for salt marsh, 'gors' = bunting), and the bird meanings are already listed.
The military officer sense is archaic and obscure and would only confuse a learner.
less militaristic is not a meaning of the word and duplicates the other meaning, goulash communism.
The 'abode of the elite' sense is a connotation of the canal belt, which is already listed, so this meaning duplicates it.
Gribus means a run-down slum area or building; 'creepy person' is not a real meaning.
Griend is a sandbank or islet (and a pilot whale is 'griend' too), but this specific species gloss duplicates the 'pilot whale' meaning.
Archaic duplicate of the other groetenis meaning, which is retained as 'greeting'.

column3: sediment at the bottom of a liquid
column4: Sediment at the bottom of a liquid duplicates the 'liquid at the bottom of a vessel' sense of grondsop (dregs).
'Primitive form' and 'principal form' are near-synonymous renderings of the same basic-form meaning, so this one is a duplicate and obscure.
Duplicates the other grondwoord meaning (root/stem of a word), which is already covered by the first entry.
The Latin subspecies name only duplicates the 'large copper' meaning.
Gup in Dutch is the guppy; 'any small fish' is a vague, overlapping sense that duplicates the guppy meaning.
'Anything small' is not a real separate sense of gup and only duplicates the other listed meanings.
Hakkelen means to stutter, not to hack (that is hakken); this meaning does not exist and the other entry covers the real sense.
Medium rare duplicates the meaning "not completely cooked" (halfgaar), which is already listed.
Duplicates the other halogeenlicht meaning, as 'light from a halogen lamp' and 'halogen light source' are essentially the same.
Physically daring is essentially a repeat of the other meanings (breakneck, acrobatic) for halsbrekend, which means dangerous or daredevil.
The gloss 'any crucial' is meaningless and this meaning (a crucial/capital case) just duplicates the other meaning, the capital-crime trial.
Duplicates the other meaning of handelstaal (business language/jargon).
The 'fast vehicle' meaning is not a real standard sense of harddraver; the word means a trotting horse, which is covered by the other entry.
Flathead mullet is just a more specific duplicate of the general 'mullet' meaning of harder.
Duplicates the meaning 'having difficulties in learning' with the archaic label, which is confusing; item 4 covers the word.
'Yard' is not a real meaning of heem and is only a spurious sense from the old Germanic root.
'Village council' is not accurate for heemraad (it is a water-board body), and it overlaps with the corrected council meaning.
Heemstede is a place name (and the 'court of law in Gelderland' sense is obscure and dubious), not useful as a common-word meaning.
A hamlet name that duplicates the place-name entry; Heemstede is chiefly a town in North Holland, so this sense only confuses learners.
This archaic religious sense is rare and overlaps with the ideal-state meaning, so it only confuses learners.
This archaic Roman-road sense is essentially a repeat of the main-road meaning and only confuses a learner.
The gloss 'bird' is too vague and the same meaning is already listed as 'hen'.
Archaic 'heul' meaning poppy is obscure (normally 'heul' is a sluice or the poppy in old texts) and would only confuse a learner.
The meaning 'stone' for 'heul' is not a real everyday meaning and is obscure at best, so it is dropped.
'Hereabout' is obscure and effectively duplicates the other meaning of hieromtrent, which a learner would only meet as 'about this'.
'Which kind of' duplicates 'what kind of', which is already listed.
Hoekbal is a hockey/handball-type term for a ball at a corner; 'corner kick' is a different word (hoekschop), so this meaning is unreliable and overlaps the other entry.
Idolatry is a figurative biblical sense of hoererij, which is already covered by the whoredom meaning, and it is obscure.
Hofmeesteres is an archaic court stewardess, not a flight attendant, and the gloss duplicates the other meaning 'stewardess'.
The 'drone' meaning is archaic and confusing, and it does not duplicate the main sense but is obscure for learners.
A hondenkot is not a hat; this meaning does not exist.
The literal 'canine dick' is a rare sense and the other entry already covers the vulgar insult, so this one is a duplicate.
Rude is practically a duplicate of insolent, so this meaning repeats another one.
The archaic 'hose' sense is obscure and only confuses learners; the word's other meanings remain.
It duplicates the 'wood carving' meaning of the other entry.
woodfree and "without wood" are the same meaning, so this duplicates the other entry.
beehive duplicates the other meaning "hive"; the chaperon meaning remains.
The archaic botanical sense "calyptra" is obscure and only confuses learners; the cape meaning remains.
Huiverig does not literally mean 'shivery' in current usage; the sense is hesitant or fearful, already covered by the other meaning.
Quivering and shiver are near-synonyms for huivering, so this duplicates item 2, which is kept.
The figurative 'barbarian' sense is obscure and the literal Hun meaning is already listed separately.
The archaic 'idiotism' duplicates the other listed meanings (idiocy and linguistic idiosyncrasy) and only confuses learners.
Idolatrous and excessively adulating are essentially the same sense, and the 'vulgar' label is wrong, so this duplicates the other meaning.
Ijs means both ice and ice cream, but ijsachtig does not specifically mean resembling ice cream; it is a dubious duplicate of the first meaning.
Tough is a vague repeat of the other meaning (stout-hearted warrior), which already covers this archaic/literary sense.
'To specify' is a rare, formal sense that overlaps with individualizing and only confuses learners.
Near-synonym of the other meaning; one entry for infaam (infamous/dishonourable) is enough, so this duplicate is dropped.
'Relating to a fire' is not a real meaning; the sense is hellish, which duplicates the diabolical meaning.
Initiate and insider are essentially the same meaning of ingewijde, so this duplicates the other entry.
Setback is not a real sense of inspringing, which means indentation, so it is a spurious duplicate of the indent meaning.
'Newcomer' essentially duplicates the 'immigrant' meaning of inwijkeling.
Javaan means a person from Java, and 'Javan' and 'person' are the same meaning, so this duplicates the other entry.
Archaic term for a jacket that merely duplicates the other meaning 'jacket'.
'Jest' and 'joke' are the same archaic meaning, so this duplicates item 3.
De jouw as a noun meaning jeer does not exist; jouw is a possessive pronoun.
'newly formed' is a rare geological sense that only confuses learners, and the main meaning 'juvenile' is already listed.
'To completely clear by plucking' repeats 'to make bald by plucking', and the figurative 'rob blind' meaning remains.
Plucking something bald is essentially the same as completely clearing it by plucking, so it duplicates the other literal meaning.
It duplicates the other meaning 'cheeseburger', which is the more natural gloss.
Fives is an English game and a poor equivalent; it duplicates the Frisian handball meaning of the same noun.
Pelote is a Basque ball game and only a near-duplicate of the Frisian handball meaning, so it would confuse a learner.
Offspring largely duplicates the other kadee meaning of kid.
'Limelike' is just a near-synonym of the other meaning 'chalky', so it duplicates it.
Archaic and obscure, and a near-duplicate of the 'package' sense, so it only confuses a learner.
Lord (of a castle) essentially duplicates castellan in entry 1.
The auction-lot sense is an obscure repeat of the existing plot and allotment meanings, so it only confuses learners.
Gloss 'relating' is meaningless and merely duplicates the Kazakh adjective meaning.
wedge mute is a nonsensical duplicate of the wedge meaning.
Eye-catching largely overlaps with fashionable and sassy as the colloquial 'kek' (stylish, striking), so it is redundant.
Kerkgezang is one concept (church singing) and this meaning duplicates the other entry, which is kept as 'hymn singing'.
Kermisklant means a funfair worker or traveller (showman); the 'customer' meaning is a wrong duplicate of the same word sense.
The truncated gloss 'any event of local' is broken and duplicates the race meaning; a kermiskoers is a local cycling race held at a fair.
The gloss 'stays' (old corset) duplicates the 'tight bodice' meaning, while 'straitjacket' (figurative constraint) is kept as the main sense.
The checkbox sense belongs to 'keuzevakje' (not 'keuzevak'), so this meaning does not exist for this word and the elective course meaning remains.
'Kieken' is a dialect form of 'kuiken/kip' that duplicates the other listed meanings (chicken, chick) and only confuses learners.
Vague gloss that duplicates the other meanings (to croak / to utter) of kikken.
Kiskassen is an obscure place name (the Casquets) that does not belong in a learner dictionary.
A klauwaard is a person, not a flag; the Flemish flag is the 'klauwaard' only by loose association, so this meaning is wrong and the other entry covers the real sense.
'Hand' is not a real meaning of klavier; it is an obscure archaic sense that only confuses learners.
The other meaning 'clayish' duplicates this one, so the second sense adds nothing.
Kleien does not mean 'to defecate'; the real senses are the clay-related ones already listed.
